The '''2026 Broxbourne Borough Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026 to elect members to [[Borough of Broxbourne|Broxbourne Borough Council]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McKiernan |first1=Jennifer |last2=Forsyth |first2=Alex |title=Twenty-nine English councils to delay elections, minister confirms |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cx2ggk333l4o |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=28 January 2026 |date=22 January 2026}}</ref> It was held on the same day as other [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|local elections]]. The election was the last election held in Broxbourne before [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|local government reorganisation]].

==Background==
In the [[2024 Broxbourne Borough Council election|2024 council election]], the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] held 9 out of 10 seats that were up for election, maintaining their majority and control of the council.<ref name="2024BBCResults">{{cite web |title=Broxbourne result - Local elections 2024 |url=http://bbc.co.uk/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000095 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=28 January 2026 |date=3 May 2024}}</ref> The [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] held the seat of Waltham Cross.<ref name="2024Results">{{cite web |last1=Stack |first1=J |title=Borough Council Election Results |url=https://www.broxbourne.gov.uk/downloads/file/4400/results-2024-borough- |publisher=[[Borough of Broxbourne|Broxbourne Borough Council]] |access-date=28 January 2026 |date=3 May 2024}}</ref> In the [[2024 United Kingdom general election|2024 general election]], [[Charles Walker (British politician)|Charles Walker]], the incumbent Conservative MP of [[Broxbourne (UK Parliament constituency)|Broxbourne]], stood down.<ref>{{cite web |title=Broxbourne's Conservative MP to quit at next election |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-beds-bucks-herts-60228532 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=28 January 2026 |date=2 February 2022}}</ref> [[Lewis Cocking]], the leader of Broxbourne Borough Council, was selected as the Conservative candidate to replace Walker and elected with a majority of 2,858 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lewis Cocking to be Broxbourne Parliamentary candidate |url=https://www.broxbourneconservatives.com/news/lewis-cocking-be-broxbourne-parliamentary-candidate |publisher=Broxbourne Conservatives |access-date=28 January 2026 |date=16 July 2023}}</ref><ref name="2024GEResults">{{cite web |title=Broxbourne - General election results 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/election/2024/uk/constituencies/E14001139 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=28 January 2026 |date=5 July 2024}}</ref> Cocking was succeeded as leader of the council by councillor Mark Mills-Bishop of Goffs Oak in May 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Printed decisions - Annual Council - Tuesday 14th May 2024 |url=https://broxbourne.moderngov.co.uk/documents/g583/Decisions%2014th-May-2024%2019.00%20Annual%20Council.pdf |publisher=[[Borough of Broxbourne|Borough of Broxbourne Council]] |access-date=15 February 2026 |date=14 May 2024}}</ref> In February 2025, councillors Giles Hall of Flamstead End and Siobhan Monaghan of Cheshunt South and Theobalds left the Conservative Party and joined [[Reform UK]]. Mills-Bishop called for Hall and Monaghan to resign and face [[by-election]]s.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Two Hertfordshire councillors defect to Reform |url=https://www.essexlive.news/news/local-news/two-hertfordshire-councillors-defect-reform-9915541 |publisher=EssexLive |access-date=28 January 2026 |date=3 February 2025}}</ref> Mills-Bishop stood down as leader in May 2025 and was succeeded by councillor Corina Gander of Goffs Oak.<ref>{{cite web |title=Leader of the Council steps down |url=https://www.broxbourne.gov.uk/news/article/376/leader-of-the-council-steps-down |publisher=[[Borough of Broxbourne|Borough of Broxbourne Council]] |access-date=15 February 2026 |date=9 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Corina Gander confirmed as new Broxbourne council leader |url=https://www.essexlive.news/news/local-news/corina-gander-confirmed-new-broxbourne-10180825 |publisher=EssexLive |access-date=15 February 2026 |date=14 May 2025}}</ref>
